comparison: Both evaluate the core lariat precursor model findings (C8, C16, C21-C23). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong biochemical evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, calling it a 'striking and new finding.' Both recognize the doubly branched product and branchpoint mutation data (C28) as key evidence, though peer review also incorporates C30-C31 and C59 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both address quantification claims (C19-C20) and plasmid system validation (C24-C25). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, treating quantification as validating intermediate presence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about 'quantitative terminology inappropriate in the absence of standard curves' and noting reliance on PCR band intensity after 35 cycles.

Both evaluate mutagenesis experiments (C26-C29). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing predictable effects consistent with lariat model. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the branchpoint mutation data and acknowledging cryptic splice site complications (C57). Both treat these as valid evidence for the mechanism.

Both address exon-skipping genes that don't circularize (C32-C33). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes limited sample size. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this as valid evidence that lariat formation alone is insufficient and that exon length matters (C34). Both treat this negative result as informative.

Both evaluate exon length effects (C36-C38, C61-C64). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing the 90 nt deletion causing >80-fold reduction and systematic relationship. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED for the deletion data itself but question whether it specifically demonstrates length versus sequence effects, suggesting additional controls needed.

Both address the comprehensive mutagenesis and exon length correlation (C9, C38). OpenEval rates this aspect SUPPORTED as part of systematic evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'the correlation of circle formation with deletion size within exon 2 seems very rough at best' and noting alternative explanations haven't been ruled out.

Both evaluate secondary structure findings (C39-C40, C68-C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the relationship between structure and circularization remains incompletely understood. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more investigation with 'finer grained mutations' and stating it would be helpful to resolve if structure truly affects circularization.

OpenEval addresses qRNA-seq quality control (C65-C67) rating SUPPORTED for technical validity. Peer reviewers incorporate these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of the exon length correlation, expressing skepticism about the overall approach despite not directly challenging the quality control data.

Both evaluate mechanistic interpretations and evolutionary speculation (C10, C41-C43, C71-C76). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but untested hypotheses extending beyond direct demonstration. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic model with appropriate caveats and acknowledging limitations about universality.

Both evaluate debranching mutant data (C44). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting global trend is supported but mrps16-specific effect doesn't reach significance. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, treating genome-wide increased circle formation as consistent with the lariat precursor hypothesis without focusing on individual gene statistics.

OpenEval includes C15 (lack of intron pairing) in broader lariat evidence evaluation rated SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C15 separately, rating SUPPORTED as contextual motivation for investigating alternative mechanisms, noting many exons lack intron pairing interactions.

OpenEval includes C17 (exon-skipping product detection) in lariat evidence rated SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C17 separately, rating SUPPORTED but noting the Exon 1-Exon 3 spliced product is not detected, presumably due to decay, and suggesting it would be nice to demonstrate this.

OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1-C7) as SUPPORTED, establishing that inverted repeats are common in mammals but rare in lower eukaryotes, justifying the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature review and established knowledge claims (C11-C14, C35, C45-C55) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and accurate representation of the field. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates minor technical details (C18, C57-C59) as SUPPORTED, including exon-skipping frequency, cryptic splicing complications, and pub1 gene structure. Peer reviewers mention C57 and C59 in other contexts but don't provide separate evaluation of these supporting details.
